claims.text: In tech-debt-register.md at stage-3, the Từ đâu ra column reads 'Có chủ ý' for N3, N4 and T1, and 'Phát hiện sau' for N1, N2 and T2.
Deliberate debt: the team knows a better shape, picks the quicker one for a stated reason and can say what it will cost, like the full copy of manifests per environment (T1).

docs/adr/0005 (written after the fact) says the team knew a better way, chose the quicker one because it had no time yet to learn a tool to build environments from one shared copy, and knew the price; register line 27: shared changes made twice; T1 repaid with Kustomize.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 docs/adr/0005-moi-moi-truong-mot-ban-manifest.md header, 'Bối cảnh', 'Quyết định', 'Hệ quả'; tech-debt-register.md line 27

claims.text: At stage-2 QueuedNotifier saved the email job in the same transaction as the order through one DbContext; the register calls this suited to one process and work to undo once Notifications became its own service; it was repaid by the outbox.
claims.source_hint: docs/team/tech-debt-register.md @ stage-3 line 28; design.l3.before-extracting-a-module summary line 3; backend.l3.outbox-pattern summary lines 1-3

claims.text: N1/N2: old notifications and payments tables remain in donhang after each service got its own database; N1's interest: a schema reader thinks the API still sends emails; both rows list PostgresFixture, the integration-test fixture, under 'Ở đâu'.
Debt can sit in data (an unused table) as well as in code.

Debt taken without anyone knowing its cost is worth preventing; review and tests are two places to catch it: review surfaces the cost to record, tests make later repayment safe. Once found it still gets a row; of the register's two labels, 'Phát hiện sau' is the nearer, though the shape never fit.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 4; management.l1.code-review-basics outline item 1; register column Từ đâu ra values

claims.text: A bug is wrong behaviour and is fixed as a defect; debt is a shape that makes correct code costlier to change. The register's lines 6-7 say code that runs wrongly is not recorded there and is fixed as a bug.
N3's reason is that older clients must not break; N4's reason is that the app runs only on a developer's machine.
claims.source_hint: docs/team/tech-debt-register.md @ stage-3 lines 20-21, column Từ đâu ra

claims.text: How a debt arrived does not change its interest but says what to check next: for deliberate debt whether the reason still holds (N3: old clients still sending unitPriceVnd); for debt found later, leftovers after the next move (N1, N2).
claims.source_hint: Lesson synthesis of outline items 1-4; register rows N1-N3 (N3 'Quyết định' column)

claims.text: Debt is measured against the changes the team makes now; sharing one DbContext was right for one process and became debt once Notifications ran on its own.
claims.source_hint: Outline misconception 2; docs/adr/0002 'Cách này đúng cho một process'; register line 28

claims.text: Automated dependency updates keep pinned versions from falling behind unnoticed, the same prevention idea applied to dependencies.
A deadline is one possible reason for debt, and some debt is not a shortcut at all (T2 and N1, found later).
